title: Closing in on Success, Performers Crave Near-Win Feedback
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This essay names and describes the 'Near-Win Effect' — a motivational surge people experience when they sense they're on the verge of succeeding — and argues leaders should deliberately leverage it with specific, encouraging feedback. Rather than vague praise, the article recommends telling performers exactly how close they are and exactly what change would close the gap, offering several sample scripts across sports, sales, and academic contexts. It closes with the counterintuitive claim that a leader doesn't need to know the precise fix; simply reinforcing belief in imminent success is often what propels performers forward.
points: Names the 'Near-Win Effect' — the motivational lift people feel when closing in on success — as a specific lever leaders can pull.
Recommends replacing generic praise with specific feedback naming exactly what stands between a performer and success.
Provides reusable example scripts across sales, sports, academics, and auditions for delivering near-win feedback.
Claims performers are unusually receptive to feedback in this window, making it a high-leverage coaching moment.
Counterintuitively argues a leader doesn't need the correct technical fix — reinforcing belief in imminent success can be enough on its own.
quotes: When performers, athletes, or team members almost achieve a desired outcome but fall just short, it is critical for leaders to provide just the right feedback that will inspire greater effort for the next performance.

Good leaders are not shy about reminding team members and teams when they are tremendously close to success. They point out the likelihood of the desired outcome and get specific as to what stands in the way.

The role of the leader in facilitating this “Near-Win Effect” is to direct their attention toward exactly what improvement or change will make the difference.

Counterintuitively, it is not always essential that the leader know exactly what will propel the team or team members forward. Great leaders know that the real victory is in believing, and they do their part to amplify that conviction.
